turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How are you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm not so good, these last few days I haven't benn able to reallykeep anything down and not feeling so good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I'm sorry to hear that. Um, when you say last few days, did you mean the past two days? 3 days?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I feel like maybe the last five days I just haven't been feeling so good and I haven't really felt like eating. But these last two days I've been really nauseous and I've thrown up a few times.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, when you say you haven't been feeling good for the past five days, is it that you feel achy? Do you feel hot like you have a fever, or do you feel weak?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I do feel hot and um, yeah, maybe a bit tired.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Tired? OK. And nausea and vomiting. Are you throwing up or just feeling nauseous?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mostly nauseous, but yeah, yesterday I threw up like three or four times and then again today I threw up like two or three times.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you throwing up any blood?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I didn't see any red. It was mostly like yellow and umm, liquidy beacuse I haven't been eating much solids or like just like food. I've been mostly just having drinks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, and so mostly fluid you said?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what color is it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhh, yeah, usually usually kind of like yellowish clear.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are you having any abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Maybe like after I vomit it kind of feels like squeezing a little bit. But I think, yeah, I think yeah that's just really just with when I'm heaving.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Right, um, are you, do you have any changes in your bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, no, I haven't noticed anything there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And so no diarrhea, no constipation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, no blood in your stool?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No blood, I haven't seen any red.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about issues swallowing food?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, no problem swallowing. Just haven't felt hungry.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so you don't have much of an appetite then.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not not really.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, alright, so um, any changes in in taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, maybe I mean, yeah, I think I might not be really tasting things the same.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about smell?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Now that you say it, I might, uh, yeah I think my smell has been impacted as well. I can't really smell anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I thought that was kind of weird, but didn't think anything of it actually until you just asked me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah for sure. And how about any changes in your vision or hearing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No changes to vision or hearing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any discharge?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, nothing like that that, but I mean my eyes were a bit, they've been a bit red these last two days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have they been in any pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope, no pain and I've been able to see everything OK. It's just I just noticed they were a little bit more red. I just thought maybe I don't know I was, I've just been tired.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah for sure. Any coughing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhh, yeah I haven't had a cough but um, I've had a cough for a few years now, so yeah, that's not really a change for me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, so no change in your cough. Is it a dry cough or a wet cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's uh, oh, a dry cough usually.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Dry cough, OK. Any blood that you produce?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No blood, no blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm not really able to exercise and stuff like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have any wheeziness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: : Um, no, I haven't had a a wheeze.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about any fatigue or tiredness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've definitely felt a little bit more kind of groggy and tired this last week, really.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and muscle aches to go along with that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, bit in my like kind of upper arms and legs a little bit.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, you said you've been feeling groggy. Do you feel dizzy at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not dizzy, just maybe that I'm like moving in slow motion.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, any confusion or memory loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think I've been OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any rashes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any rashes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, these last few days I've had a bit of a headache as well.It hasn't been very intense, so, um, I'm not worried about it too much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Right, OK. It hasn't been intense you said? So have you had headaches like this in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I had similar headaches before I think. They come like this. Like if I didn't get a good sleep or from not drinking enough water or something, I'll kind of get a headache like this. Kind of feels like it's squeezing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, that's understandable. But it's not like the worst headache you've ever had?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, it's pretty similar to headaches that I've had before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, good, and are you otherwise healthy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, well I have high blood pressure and also, high cholesterol, so I do take medications for both of those. So yeah, I take a statin and Amlodipine I think.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, good. It's good that you're on both of those. Do you take any other medications like over the counter medications or herbal supplements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've been taking vitamin D and also a multivitamin. I heard that that we don't get enough vitamin D throughout the winter.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, it's a great idea to take that, especially as we get older and if we live in a country where we don't get a lot of sun exposure like Canada, so that's good. And sorry before I move on, I forgot to ask you earlier if you have experienced any weight loss or night sweats recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, my weight's been, uh, about the same unfortunately and I haven't had any night sweats. But I mean now that you asked if I felt more hot than than usual, maybe.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and did you take your temperature?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I did and the last time I checked it was a few days ago and at that time I didn't have a fever, but I mean, I'm still feeling hot so I'm not sure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, OK. Alright, so I'll go back to your past medical history. Have you been hospitalized or have you ever needed surgeries in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no. Like the last time I was in the hospital with, it was for a colonoscopy a few years ago which came back normal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that's good. Um, are you up to date with all your immunizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah, actually got the shingles vaccine a few months ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably closer to a year ago now, actually.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Oh great, OK, that's awesome and are you allergic to anything?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just peanuts.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Peanuts, OK. Do you know if you have a family history of any lung or heart conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, my son has asthma. But nobody in my family's had a heart problem, though.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about any stomach problems or liver problems? Colon problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, my dad actually had colon cancer. He was 70 and so that's why we went and decided to get a colonoscopy instead of just doing the immunohistochemistry test.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah, that's a good idea. Um, so it sounds like you're, you know, preemptive with your health, which is good. Any other cancers that run in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, just my dad had colon cancer.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And do you smoke at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no, I don't smoke marijuana.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about other recreational drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I mean, I briefly like dabbled in the past at parties and stuff like that but that was when I was way younger, like in in my college years.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, what kind of drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think maybe we used cocaine a few times and MDMA, uh, but that was like a long time, probably like 30 years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, were any of these drugs injected IV?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, I've never done that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, that's good. Do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I have like maybe I don't know a couple of drinks a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that's good. What kind of drinks do you have and how much of it do you have?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Usually, it'll just be one or two glasses of wine at a time and maybe two nights a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: And I usually stick with red wine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, great, and who do you live with?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So um, it's just me and my son.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How old is your son?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, he's 18.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you live in a house or an apartment?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah, we live in an apartment. Yeah, on the 8th floor.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: On the 8th floor, OK, any issues in terms of like old carpet or mold or asbestos in the apartment?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's a newish building so there isn't really any carpet actually in the unit, so yeah, it's pretty clean that way.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK good. That's good. So those were all the questions that I had for you. Did you have any questions or concerns that you wanted to bring up before we ended the interview?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I'm just hoping to to get this sorted out and feel better.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah for sure. So you know, right now we're thinking it could be a viral GI viral infection because of your complaints of nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite and fever. But it could also be COVID and we are going to have to do a swab for you and run that test because you have a lot of symptoms that overlap with those symptoms. Um, and then, so just going off of that, we'll wait for the swabs to come back. If they come back positive, we will notify public health and they'll do a trace to see where you could have gotten this infection from. And then meanwhile, we do suggest that you isolate for two weeks so that you don't spread the illness, and even if the swab comes back negative, there is still a chance that you may have COVID and it's a false negative test. So we'll start there. If it turns out you don't have any of those viral illnesses and you have more of a, you know, bacterial picture, we can work you up for that and prescribe antibiotics. So that's where we will start. How does that sound?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds like a great start. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, great.
